text.p: Adelaide Bank Ltd said on Thursday it had a further A$200 million securitisation tranche planned for around April or May of 1997.
"We have got another tranche of A$200 million planned for around about April/May next year," managing director Barry Fitzpatrick told reporters after the bank's annual meeting.

Fitzpatrick said the bank's current performance was looking very good. "We are very pleased with the first quarter results and we expect to announce another very good year for Adelaide Bank," he said. "The first quarter is up (on last year)," he said, adding he believed shareholders would be very happy with the company's half-year results.
Asked if the A$200 million tranche would be the last for 1996/97, Fitzpatrick said: "It depends how we go."
"We have the flexibility now to issue tranches fairly quickly through the Torrens Trust and a lot will depend on how our marketing strategies go interstate," he said.

Fitzpatrick said he believed the Reserve Bank was in the final stages of making its decision on whether Adelaide Bank can retain Co-operative Retirement Services, a legacy from its building society days.
The division, which owns or manages 39 retirement estates in Australia, contributed net profit in 1995/96 of A$1.86 million.
"We understand that (the Reserve) are sympathetic but they have not made a final determination yet," he said.
"I am still very hopeful we will be allowed to keep our villages because they are a good contribitor to after tax profits of the bank," he said.
Fitzpatrick said all banks' margins would come under pressure following the recent cut in official interest rates.
"I think it is a matter of the flow-on effect to assets and liabilities which will see Adelaide Bank's margin remain relatively stable as it is now," he said.
Fitzpatrick said the home loan market would still be viable in future for regional banks, but banks generally would decide on what component of the housing loan they would focus.
"You will not be all things for all people, you will do some parts, you will outsource some, and you may even do transactional processing for other organisations," he said.
As part of Adelaide Bank's move to boost its retirement, treasury and insurance operations, Fitzpatrick said an announcement would be made by NZI Insurance next week.
Earlier, chairman Richard Fidock told shareholders the bank believed fee based income must move from its current level of around 20 percent of income to around 40 percent.
"No longer can any bank, Adelaide Bank included, have a situation where those with housing, investment or business loans are subsidising transactions initiated by others," he said.
Fidock said the bank was looking forward to another strong performance in 1996/97 in what would be a year of great change.
